ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the sector $ABC$ with a radius of $6$, where $\angle AOB = 120^\circ$, $C$ is a moving point on the arc $\overset{\frown}{AB}$ (not coinciding with $A$ or $B$), $OD \perp AC$, $OE \perp BC$, with the feet of the perpendiculars being points $D$ and $E$, respectively. Find the measures of each interior angle of the quadrilateral $ODCE$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As the figure shows, take a point $H$ on the major arc $AB$, and connect $AH$, $BH$, \\
$\therefore \angle AHB=\frac{1}{2}\angle AOB=60^\circ$, \\
$\because$ quadrilateral $ACBH$ is a cyclic quadrilateral, \\
$\therefore \angle DCE=180^\circ-\angle AHB=\boxed{120^\circ}$, \\
$\because OD\perp AC$, $OE\perp BC$, \\
$\therefore \angle ODC=\angle OEC=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle BOD=360^\circ-\angle ODC-\angle OEC-\angle DCE=\boxed{60^\circ}$;

Reasoning: Since D lies on AC and E lies on BC, the angle at C of quadrilateral ODCE is ∠DCE = ∠ACB. Point C is on the minor arc AB, so the inscribed angle ∠ACB intercepts the major arc AB. Given ∠AOB = 120°, the major arc AB has measure 360° - 120° = 240°. Therefore ∠ACB = 1/2 × 240° = 120°, so ∠DCE = 120°. Also, OD ⟂ AC gives ∠ODC = 90°, and OE ⟂ BC gives ∠OEC = 90°. The interior angles of quadrilateral ODCE sum to 360°, so ∠DOE = 360° - 90° - 120° - 90° = 60°.

Find the measures of each interior angle of quadrilateral $ODCE$.
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer: Solution: As shown in the figure, take a point $H$ on the major arc $AB$, and connect $AH$ and $BH$. Therefore $\angle AHB = \frac{1}{2}\angle AOB = 60^\circ$. Because quadrilateral $ACBH$ is cyclic, $\angle DCE = 180^\circ - \angle AHB = 120^\circ$. Because $OD \perp AC$ and $OE \perp BC$, $\angle ODC = \angle OEC = 90^\circ$. Therefore $\angle BOD = 360^\circ - \angle ODC - \angle OEC - \angle DCE = 60^\circ$.
